# Bacteria and Archaea


## 1. Methods

Data was evaluated with fastqc and determined to have little nextera
transposase adapter contamination. Data was run through Nephele's QC
pipeline (updated December 2025) for adapter trimming. Trimmed data was
passed through WGSA2 pipeline in Nephele where it was decontaminated for human and mouse reads. 
Read counts were used in this analysis. Batch correction was performed to adjust for cage because that had the greatest effect on microbial composition and co-varied with experiment. The counts were converted to relative abundance because the rarefaction curves did not reach the asymptote and some did not hit inflection point as much as I would like to see. I used chao1 as the richness metric because it estimates rare taxa we may be missing, versus observed species (raw data was used). 

The main fixed effect was Treatment (treated versus control) but also did the analysis with the breakdown of H20 and BSS timepoint. Alpha diversity was evaluated with confounders - cage, experiment, subject - and without.
I also did differential abundance with rarefied reads (to 2850000) just to see how different the results were with a different normalization method. 

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(stringr)

library(metagMisc)
library(vegan)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggpubr)

library(GUniFrac)
library(ggrepel)

library(RColorBrewer)
library(scales)
library(ggtext)

library(downloadthis)
library(kableExtra)

library(ampvis2)
```

## 2. Data processing 

### Import data and create phyloseq object. 

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

data<-read.csv("mouse_metagenome_taxa_bact-arch.csv", row.names=1, header=TRUE)


taxa <- data[, c("kingdom","phylum","class","order","family","genus","species","OTU")]
data[, c("kingdom","phylum","class","order","family","genus","species","OTU","ATCCMSA2002control_P1","ATCCMSA2002control_P2","NegativeControl","NegativeControl_P2")] <- NULL 

```


```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
metadata<-read.csv("metadata.csv", row.names=1, header=TRUE) 

metadata$Timepoint <- factor(metadata$Timepoint,
    levels = c('Day 0', 'Day 3'),ordered = TRUE)


otu<-otu_table(data, taxa_are_rows=TRUE)
meta<-sample_data(metadata)
tax<-tax_table(as.matrix(taxa))
phylo_raw<-phyloseq(otu, meta, tax)
phylo_raw_df<-phyloseq_to_df(phylo_raw, addtax=F)
rownames(phylo_raw_df)<-phylo_raw_df[,1]
phylo_raw_df<-dplyr::select(phylo_raw_df, -c("OTU"))
metadata<-data.frame(sample_data(phylo_raw))
phylo_raw_df<-as.data.frame(t(phylo_raw_df))
#pairwise.adonis2(phylo_raw_df~SequenceRun, data=metadata)

phylo_raw


```

### Batch correction

There were differences in sequencing run, so will batch correct. 

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}


phylo_raw_df<-as.data.frame(t(phylo_raw_df))
fit_adjust_batch <- adjust_batch(feature_abd = phylo_raw_df,
                                batch = "Cage..",
                                data = metadata,
                                control = list(verbose = FALSE))

CRC_abd_adj <- fit_adjust_batch$feature_abd_adj 

otu2<-otu_table(CRC_abd_adj, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
meta<-sample_data(metadata)
tax<-tax_table(as.matrix(taxa))

phylo_adj<-phyloseq(otu2, meta, tax)

```

### Filtering

Filtered for prevalence (10%) and abundance (count of 10) instead of critical value to increase number of taxa analyzed. Both must be true to pass filter. 

```{r}


#critical_value <- 0.00001*sum(taxa_sums(phylo_raw))
#phylo <- filter_taxa(phylo_raw, function(x) sum(x) > critical_value, TRUE)
#phylo

phylo<-phyloseq_filter_prevalence(phylo_adj, abund.trh=10, prev.trh=0.10, abund.type="total", threshold_condition ="AND")
phylo

summary(sample_sums(phylo))

```

<br>

### Rarefaction curve

Evaluating the number of reads to rarefy to to normalization for differences in sequencing depth. 

```{r message=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

summary(sample_sums(phylo))

phylo_df<-phyloseq_to_df(phylo_raw, addtax=F)
rownames(phylo_df)<-phylo_df[,1]
phylo_df<-dplyr::select(phylo_df, -c("OTU"))

library(ampvis2) 
metadata<-read.csv("metadata.csv")
#phylo_df<-as.data.frame(t(phylo_df))
y<-amp_load(phylo_df, metadata, taxa)

rarecurve<-amp_rarecurve(
  y,
  stepsize = 10000,
  color_by = NULL,
  facet_by = "Timepoint",
  facet_scales = "free_x"
) + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0, 10000000))
rarecurve

#ggexport(rarecurve, filename="species_rarecurve.pdf", width=8, height=6)

```



```{r message=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
genus_pre_rare<-tax_glom(phylo_raw, "genus")
genus_pre_df<-phyloseq_to_df(genus_pre_rare, addtax=T)
rownames(genus_pre_df)<-genus_pre_df[,"genus"]
genus_pre_df<-dplyr::select(genus_pre_df, -c("kingdom","phylum","order","class","family","genus","species","OTU","OTU.1"))

y<-amp_load(genus_pre_df, metadata)

rarecurve<-amp_rarecurve(
  y,
  stepsize = 10000,
  color_by = NULL,
  facet_by = "Timepoint",
  facet_scales = "free_x"
) + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0, 10000000))
rarecurve

#ggexport(rarecurve, filename="genus_rarecurve.pdf", width=8, height=6)

```

<br>

> Notes: At both species and genus level, we don't really reach the asmpytote. Genus is better, but this is likely undersampled.  

<br><br>

### Normalization

Due to likely undersampling, I didn't want to lose any taxa so I used relative abundance for normalization. 

```{r}
#dada2_rare_0 <- rarefy_even_depth(phylo, sample.size = 2850000, replace=F, rngseed=123)

#rarefied<-phyloseq_to_df(dada2_rare_0, addtax=F)
#rownames(rarefied)<-rarefied[,1]
#rarefied<-dplyr::select(rarefied, -c("OTU"))
#write.csv(rarefied, "rarefied_bacterial_table_not_batch_filtered_prev.csv")

norm_phylo<-normalize(phylo, method="relative")

phylo_df<-phyloseq_to_df(norm_phylo, addtax=F)
rownames(phylo_df)<-phylo_df[,1]
phylo_df<-dplyr::select(phylo_df, -c("OTU"))


```

### Calculating alpha diversity

Calculated for both species and genus level from raw data (not filtered) since it was undersampled. 

```{r}

## calculate alpha diversity


phy_alphadiv <- estimate_richness(phylo_adj)
otu_table <- otu_table(t(phylo_adj))
evenness<- diversity(otu_table)/log(specnumber(otu_table))
chao1 <- t(estimateR(otu_table))[,2]
all_alphadivs <- data.frame(phy_alphadiv, evenness, chao1)
update_sample_data <- merge(sample_data(phylo_adj), all_alphadivs, by=0)
rownames(update_sample_data) <- update_sample_data$Row.names
update_sample_data$Row.names <- NULL
sample_data(phylo_adj) <- update_sample_data
metadata<-update_sample_data

genus_norm_adj<-tax_glom(phylo_adj, "genus") 

phy_alphadiv <- estimate_richness(genus_norm_adj)
otu_table <- otu_table(t(genus_norm_adj))
evenness<- diversity(otu_table)/log(specnumber(otu_table))
chao1 <- t(estimateR(otu_table))[,2]
all_alphadivs <- data.frame(phy_alphadiv, evenness, chao1)
update_sample_data <- merge(sample_data(genus_norm_adj), all_alphadivs, by=0)
rownames(update_sample_data) <- update_sample_data$Row.names
update_sample_data$Row.names <- NULL
sample_data(genus_norm_adj) <- update_sample_data
metadata_genus<-update_sample_data


genus_norm<-tax_glom(norm_phylo, "genus")
genus_df<-phyloseq_to_df(genus_norm, addtax=T)
rownames(genus_df)<-genus_df[,"genus"]
genus_df<-dplyr::select(genus_df, -c("kingdom","phylum","order","class","family","genus","species","OTU","OTU.1"))



```

```{r}

all_alphadivs %>% kable(caption="<center><strong>Table X. Alpha diversity (genus).<center><strong>") %>% kable_styling() %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T)

```

## 3. Effectors and Interactions 

Looked for possible effectors or interacting variables. Cage, experiment. 

## Species

### Cage

```{r}

result<-adonis2(phyloseq::distance(norm_phylo, method="bray") ~ sample_data(norm_phylo)$Cage..)

result<-result[1,c(3,5)]

result$Comparison<-"Cage"
rownames(result)<-result$Comparison

kable(result[,c(1,2)], caption="Table X. PERMANOVA results for investigating differences in bacterial composition.", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:60%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"))

```
```{r}
ord_filt_subject<- ordinate(norm_phylo, "MDS", "bray")  
all_pcoa_subject1 <- plot_ordination(norm_phylo, ord_filt_subject, type = "site", 
                                   color = "Cage..") + 
  geom_point(size = 4) + theme_bw()

all_pcoa_subject1
```

<br>

### Experiment

```{r}

result<-adonis2(phyloseq::distance(norm_phylo, method="bray") ~ sample_data(norm_phylo)$Experiment.source)

result<-result[1,c(3,5)]

result$Comparison<-"Experiment"
rownames(result)<-result$Comparison

kable(result[,c(1,2)], caption="Table X. PERMANOVA results for investigating differences in bacterial composition.", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:60%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"))

```

```{r}

ord_filt_subject<- ordinate(norm_phylo, "MDS", "bray")  

all_pcoa_subject1 <- plot_ordination(norm_phylo, ord_filt_subject, type = "site", 
                                   color = "Experiment.source") + 
  geom_point(size = 4) + theme_bw()

all_pcoa_subject1
```

<br>

> Notes: Cage and experiment are strongly associated with microbial community composition. 

<br><br>

## 4. Beta diversity

Differences between time point using PERMANOVA at genus level.

### Time and Treatment 

#### Bray-Curtis

```{r}

genus_df<-as.data.frame(t(genus_df))
bray<-pairwise.adonis2(genus_df~Time_Treatment, data=metadata)

results_df <- do.call(rbind, bray)
results_df <- results_df[grepl("Model", rownames(results_df)), ]
results_df$Comparison<-rownames(results_df)
results_df<- results_df %>% mutate(Comparison = gsub(".Model", "", Comparison))
rownames(results_df)<-results_df$Comparison

results_df<-results_df %>% mutate_at(1:5, as.numeric)
results_df[c(1:5)] <- lapply(results_df[c(1:5)], round, digits = 3)

results_df[,c(1,2,6)]<-NULL
results_df %>% kable(caption="<strong>Table X. Differences in bacterial species composition using Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity.<strong>", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:80%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped"))%>%
   column_spec(4, color=ifelse(results_df[,3] < 0.05, "green","black"))


library(downloadthis)
results_df %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "PERMANOVAresults-bacteria-bray",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )

```

```{r}

ord_filt_subject<- ordinate(genus_norm, "MDS", "bray")  

all_pcoa_subject1 <- plot_ordination(genus_norm, ord_filt_subject, type = "site", 
                                   color = "Time_Treatment") + 
  geom_point(size = 4) + theme_bw()

all_pcoa_subject1


all_pcoa_subject1 %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "PCOA_bacteria_bray",
    output_extension = ".pdf",
    button_label = "Download figure as .pdf",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa-solid fa-image",
    ggsave_args = list(height=4, width=6)
  )
```

<br>

```{r}

## 6. Differential abundance: Genus

```{r results=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}

library(Maaslin2)


subject_all = Maaslin2(
  input_data = genus_df,
  input_metadata = metadata,
  output = "Treated_genus",
  fixed_effects = c('Control.or.Treated'), normalization="NONE", random_effect=c("Subject.ID","Experiment.source","Cage.."), analysis_method="LM", transform="LOG", plot_scatter = FALSE)

LM<-subject_all$results


## re-install maaslin2 to fix package error. Log transform with linear model? 

table<-as.data.frame(LM[,c("feature","value","coef","qval","N.not.zero")])

table_sub<- table %>% filter(qval < 0.20)
table_sub2<- table_sub %>% filter(coef< -1)
table_sub3<- table_sub %>% filter(coef > 1)
table_sub4_day0<-rbind(table_sub2, table_sub3)
table_sub4_day0$genus<-table_sub4_day0$feature
taxa[,c("species","OTU")]<-NULL
taxa_uniq<-data.frame(unique(taxa))
DAA_taxa<-merge.data.frame(table_sub4_day0, taxa_uniq, by="genus", all.x=TRUE, all.y=FALSE)
#write.csv(DAA_taxa, "DAA_genus.csv")


```

```{r}



dust(DAA_taxa) %>%
  kable(caption = "<strong>Table X. Differentially abundant bacterial genera in treated compared to control. Results show q val < 0.2. <strong>") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped")) %>% column_spec(column=3, width_min="5em", include_thead = T) %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T) 

library(downloadthis)
DAA_taxa %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "Differentally abundant bacterial genera",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )

```


<br><br>


#### Genus barchart

```{r}

DAA_taxa<- DAA_taxa %>% filter(qval < 0.05)

nb.cols<-21
mycolors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nb.cols)

#table(DAA_taxa$phylum)

#DAA_taxa$phylum<- factor(DAA_taxa$phylum,
   # levels = c('Bacillota','Fusobacteriota','Pseudomonadota'), ordered = TRUE)

DAA_taxa$genus <- factor(DAA_taxa$genus, levels = DAA_taxa$genus[order(DAA_taxa$phylum, decreasing=TRUE)])


#mycolors <- c("#2D82AF","#FE982C","#D9A295")

DAA_taxa<- DAA_taxa %>% mutate(updated_text = gsub("_", " ", genus))



DAA_taxa$updated_text<- factor(DAA_taxa$updated_text, levels = DAA_taxa$updated_text[order(DAA_taxa$phylum, DAA_taxa$coef, decreasing=TRUE)])

stacked_species<-ggplot(DAA_taxa, aes(x = coef, y = updated_text, fill=phylum)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",show.legend = TRUE) + xlab("Effect size") +scale_fill_manual(values=mycolors)+theme_classic()+geom_col(color="black")+theme(legend.position="right") +ylab(NULL) +guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 21))


#stacked_species
#ggexport(stacked_species, filename="Stacked_plot_species.pdf", width=6, height=9)

DAA_taxa$qval_adj<--log10(DAA_taxa$qval)

bubble_species<-ggplot(DAA_taxa, aes(x=value, y=updated_text, size = qval_adj)) + geom_point(alpha=1, aes(color=phylum))+scale_size(range=c(0.01,4), "-log10(p value)")+scale_color_manual(values=mycolors)+theme_void()+guides(color="none", fill="none")

#bubble_species
```

<br><br>


```{r fig.cap="**Figure X. Differentially abundant genera (effect size > 1 or <  - 1) colored by phylum after treatment compared to contols.. Significance represents -log10 of adjusted p value after multiple comparisons (< 0.05). The greater the circle the more statistically significant.**", fig.height=20, fig.width=12}

figure<-stacked_species+bubble_species

figure


library(downloadthis)
figure %>%
  download_this(

### Time/Treatment


```{r}


genus_df<-phyloseq_to_df(genus_norm, addtax=T)

fit <- lmer(Enterococcus~Time_Treatment + (1|Subject.ID)+(1|Cage..)+(1|Experiment.source), data = metadata_genus)

emmeans<-summary(emmeans(fit, pairwise~Time_Treatment))
summary<-data.frame(emmeans$contrasts)
summary <- summary %>% separate(contrast, c('group1', 'group2'), sep=" - ")

summary$p<-round(summary$`p.value`, digits = 3)
summary$y.position<-0.11

summary

Entero_plot1<-ggplot(metadata_genus, aes(Time_Treatment, Enterococcus)) +geom_boxplot(aes(middle = mean(Enterococcus), color=Time_Treatment, fill=Time_Treatment), outlier.shape=NA, color="black")+geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height=0, seed=1), size=1, color="black")+labs(x=NULL, title="Enterococcus")+theme_bw() + ylab("Relative abundance")+theme(axis.text.x=element_text(size=10, angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.text.y=element_text(size=10), axis.title=element_text(size=12), plot.title = element_text(size=12), legend.position="none")+ scale_colour_brewer(type="qual", palette="Paired") +scale_fill_brewer(type="qual", palette="Paired")+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,0.12))
Entero_plot1

## 9. Differential abundance: rarefied 

Rarefied at 2850000 to compare results. 

```{r}

dada2_rare_0 <- rarefy_even_depth(phylo, sample.size = 2850000, replace=F, rngseed=123)

rarefied<-phyloseq_to_df(dada2_rare_0, addtax=F)
rownames(rarefied)<-rarefied[,1]
rarefied<-dplyr::select(rarefied, -c("OTU"))

genus_rare<-tax_glom(dada2_rare_0, "genus")
rarefied_genus<-phyloseq_to_df(genus_rare, addtax=T)
rownames(rarefied_genus)<-rarefied_genus[,"genus"]
rarefied_genus<-dplyr::select(rarefied_genus, -c("kingdom","phylum","class","order","family","genus","species","OTU","OTU.1"))

```


```{r results=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}

library(Maaslin2)

subject_all = Maaslin2(
  input_data = rarefied_genus,
  input_metadata = metadata,
  output = "Treated_genus_rarefied",
  fixed_effects = c('Control.or.Treated'), normalization="NONE", random_effect=c("Subject.ID", "Experiment.source","Cage.."), analysis_method="LM", transform="LOG", plot_scatter = FALSE)

LM<-subject_all$results


## re-install maaslin2 to fix package error. Log transform with linear model? 

table<-as.data.frame(LM[,c("feature","value","coef","qval","N.not.zero")])

table_sub<- table %>% filter(qval < 0.20)
table_sub2<- table_sub %>% filter(coef< -1)
table_sub3<- table_sub %>% filter(coef > 1)
table_sub4_day0<-rbind(table_sub2, table_sub3)
table_sub4_day0$genus<-table_sub4_day0$feature
taxa[,c("species","OTU")]<-NULL
taxa_uniq<-data.frame(unique(taxa))
DAA_taxa<-merge.data.frame(table_sub4_day0, taxa_uniq, by="genus", all.x=TRUE, all.y=FALSE)
#write.csv(DAA_taxa, "DAA_genus.csv")


```

```{r}



dust(DAA_taxa) %>%
  kable(caption = "<strong>Table X. Differentially abundant bacterial genera in treated compared to control. Results show q value < 0.2.<strong>") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped")) %>% column_spec(column=3, width_min="5em", include_thead = T) %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T) 

library(downloadthis)
DAA_taxa %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "Differentally abundant bacterial genera",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )

```

#### Genus barchart

```{r}

DAA_taxa<- DAA_taxa %>% filter(qval < 0.05)

nb.cols<-13
mycolors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nb.cols)

DAA_taxa$genus <- factor(DAA_taxa$genus, levels = DAA_taxa$genus[order(DAA_taxa$phylum, decreasing=TRUE)])


#mycolors <- c("#2D82AF","#98D277","#FE982C","#D9A295","purple")

DAA_taxa<- DAA_taxa %>% mutate(updated_text = gsub("_", " ", genus))

DAA_taxa$updated_text<- factor(DAA_taxa$updated_text, levels = DAA_taxa$updated_text[order(DAA_taxa$phylum, DAA_taxa$coef, decreasing=TRUE)])

stacked_species<-ggplot(DAA_taxa, aes(x = coef, y = updated_text, fill=phylum)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",show.legend = TRUE) + xlab("Effect size") +scale_fill_manual(values=mycolors)+theme_classic()+geom_col(color="black")+theme(legend.position="right") +ylab(NULL)

#stacked_species
#ggexport(stacked_species, filename="Stacked_plot_species.pdf", width=6, height=9)

DAA_taxa$qval_adj<--log10(DAA_taxa$qval)

bubble_species<-ggplot(DAA_taxa, aes(x=value, y=updated_text, size = qval_adj)) + geom_point(alpha=1, aes(color=phylum))+scale_size(range=c(0.01,4), "-log10(p value)")+scale_color_manual(values=mycolors)+theme_void()+guides(color="none", fill="none")

#bubble_species
```

<br><br>


```{r fig.cap="**Figure X. Differentially abundant genera (effect size > 1 or <  - 1) colored by phylum after treatment compared to contols.. Significance represents -log10 of adjusted p value after multiple comparisons (< 0.05). The greater the circle the more statistically significant.**", fig.height=9, fig.width=8}


figure<-stacked_species+bubble_species

figure


library(downloadthis)
figure %>%
  download_this(
